data.narrative:
Stacked Energy, a Series A climate and energy technology company founded by Dylan Erb and Sumitha Durairaj, has raised $98M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 companies in the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (Linzatech, ticker LNZA) and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy frontier-tech band; fewer than three datapoints survived filtering. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to series transition dynamics. Using the $98M total raised as a valuation proxy, this method implies a $196M post-money valuation.

The triangulated range spans $167M (low) to $225M (high), centered on $196M. The median reflects the single applicable method and should be interpreted with caution given reliance on one approach and the absence of directly comparable same-stage peers. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier in an illiquid frontier-tech market and the precise timing and stage definition of comparable financings. Additional data on recent Climate & Energy Series A round sizes and valuations would strengthen conviction in this range.
